# Independent code review iteration

Scope: independent full pass over `octolab/pkg` at `22a5242` (2022-03-09): all non-generated Go packages and tests, module/tool metadata, CI, lint configuration, and public docs. Existing review files were not read as review input; overlap with prior reviews is intentional independent corroboration. Offline issue and roadmap dumps were excluded.

Validation: `GOFLAGS=-mod=readonly go test -race ./...` was run on Go 1.26.5 and **failed** in `go.octolab.org/errors` with eight classification assertions; all other tested packages passed. `GOFLAGS=-mod=readonly go vet ./...` passed. Findings 1 and the current incompatibility are therefore dynamically reproduced, not inferred from age alone.

Class: `correctness` · `security` · `concurrency` · `perf` · `api` · `idiom` · `modern` · `test` · `build` · `docs`.

## 1. Unwrap erases terminal errors that expose an empty unwrap slot

`errors.Unwrap` repeatedly assigns `err = layer.Unwrap()` until the value no longer implements `Unwrap`. If an error type implements `Unwrap() error` but returns nil, the function returns nil instead of the last non-nil error. This is now common: `net.DNSError` has an optional `UnwrapErr`, and a normal DNS error with no inner cause reports nil.

`Classifier.Classify` immediately calls this helper and treats nil as `Unknown`. On Go 1.26.5, the repository's own `TestClassifier_ClassifyAs` fails for wrapped network, temporary, and timeout cases (eight assertions). The `1.x` CI lane would therefore be red even before considering obsolete Actions.

**Fix.** Do not flatten the chain before classification. Use `errors.Is` / `errors.As` on the original error. If a root-cause helper is still required, retain `current` and stop when `next := errors.Unwrap(current)` is nil, returning `current`. Add regression tests for `DNSError{UnwrapErr:nil}` and a custom optional wrapper.

## 2. A legal short read truncates and prematurely rewinds the body

`repeatable.Read` treats `n < len(p) && err == nil` as end-of-stream. The `io.Reader` contract explicitly permits a reader to return any positive `n` with nil error while more bytes remain. In that case this wrapper replaces the source with the bytes seen so far, returns `io.EOF`, and permanently loses the unread suffix. Network, throttled, and chunked readers can all produce such reads.

The existing tests use `strings.Reader`, `bytes.Reader`, and a regular file; none simulates repeated small reads, so they cannot expose the truncation.

**Fix.** Rotate only after an actual `io.EOF`. Preserve `(n > 0, io.EOF)` semantics by delivering the bytes and rotating for the next call. Add a reader that returns one byte with nil error per call and verify several complete replays.

## 3. A failing error handler can leave Wait blocked forever

`Job.Do` calls `WaitGroup.Done` after the action succeeds, or after `handler(err)` returns. If the action returns an error while `handler` is nil, or if the handler panics, `Done` is never reached and `Job.Wait()` blocks indefinitely. The success examples pass nil handlers, making accidental error returns especially hazardous.

**Fix.** Start the goroutine with `defer wg.Done()` so accounting is unconditional. Make the handler optional (`if handler != nil`) and define whether handler panics should be recovered or deliberately crash the process. Prefer `errgroup.Group` when errors need aggregation.

## 4. Dependency-only pull requests skip the code workflow

The workflow uses the literal pattern `go.{mod,sum}`. GitHub path filters document `*`, `**`, `?`, character classes, and `+`; they do not perform shell brace expansion. The pattern therefore matches a file literally named `go.{mod,sum}`, not `go.mod` or `go.sum`. Dependabot's root-module updates can bypass lint, tests, and race detection.

**Fix.** Replace it in both event blocks with separate `go.mod` and `go.sum` entries. Add the root Makefile and generated-code inputs that affect compilation. Reference: [GitHub path pattern syntax](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax#patterns-to-match-file-paths).

## 5. The coverage workflow uses an artifact transport that now hard-fails

The Go 1.19 lane uploads coverage with `actions/upload-artifact@v3`, and `report` downloads it with `actions/download-artifact@v3`. GitHub.com stopped accepting v3 on 30 January 2025, so otherwise green tests still produce a failed workflow and no coverage upload.

**Fix.** Upgrade both ends to v4 in the same change, then update checkout/setup-go/cache and Codecov. Re-run the entire matrix manually. Reference: [GitHub's artifact v3 shutdown notice](https://github.blog/changelog/2024-04-16-deprecation-notice-v3-of-the-artifact-actions/).

## 6. Environment restoration can deadlock the remaining test suite

`SetEnvs` acquires a package-global mutex and deliberately keeps it locked until the caller invokes the returned rollback closure. Any `require.*`, panic, `Goexit`, or early return between setup and rollback leaves the mutex locked forever; the next test calling `SetEnvs` hangs. The API example calls `release` manually rather than with `defer`/`Cleanup`, so it teaches the unsafe lifecycle. Duplicate keys are also restored incorrectly because `before[key]` is overwritten after the first mutation.

**Fix.** Accept `testing.TB`, register restoration with `tb.Cleanup`, and use `t.Setenv` on supported Go versions. If this helper remains, reject duplicate keys, make rollback idempotent, and document that process environment cannot be safely mutated by genuinely parallel tests.

## 7. Watch callbacks execute while the registry read lock is held

The watcher holds `RLock` while invoking every user callback. A callback that calls `Watch` or `Forget` needs the write lock and deadlocks itself. A slow callback also blocks all registry updates and delays cancellation. The panic path manually unlocks inside a distant error handler, coupling lock balance to `safe.Do` implementation details.

**Fix.** Copy the callbacks under `RLock`, unlock, then invoke the snapshot. Recover per callback if isolation is desired, and stop the ticker with a defer owned by the worker goroutine.

## 8. Invalid batch sizes panic inside a public helper

`Range(size, batch)` divides by `batch` without validating it. `batch == 0` panics with divide-by-zero; negative size/batch combinations can produce a negative slice length. A batching helper should not turn user-provided configuration into a process crash without an explicit contract.

**Fix.** Return `(bounds []int, err error)` and reject negative size or non-positive batch, or document and enforce a panic with a clear message. Add boundary tests for zero and negative inputs.

## 9. ParseSize accepts non-finite and non-positive quantities

The documented error says the value must be a positive integer, but parsing uses `ParseFloat` and rejects only `bytes < 0`. Consequently `0B`, fractions, `NaNB`, and `InfB` pass the validation; non-finite or overflowing float-to-uint conversions yield meaningless `Size` values. Large finite inputs can also overflow after multiplying by the unit.

**Fix.** Decide whether fractions are supported and align the contract. Reject `<= 0`, `math.IsNaN`, `math.IsInf`, and values above `math.MaxUint64/unit` before conversion. Add fuzz/property tests around unit boundaries.

## 10. UUID generation silently converts entropy failure into duplication

`UUID.Next` discards `uuid.NewRandom` errors and returns the receiver. Calling it on a previous ID repeats that ID; calling it on zero returns an invalid empty value. Downstream code cannot tell an entropy failure from a generated identifier, so a transient OS failure becomes duplicate primary keys or overwritten records.

**Fix.** Return `(UUID, error)` and propagate the randomness failure. If a Must-style helper is valuable, expose it separately and panic explicitly rather than returning stale state.

## 11. The package surface and toolchain have no current support policy

The root module declares Go 1.13, tools are pinned to 2022-era forks, CI stops at Go 1.19 plus a floating `1.x`, and many packages duplicate APIs now present in modern Go (`atomic` types, `slices`, `cmp`, `io.NopCloser`, `signal.NotifyContext`, `testing.T.Setenv`). The current test failure demonstrates that a floating lane without maintenance is not compatibility.

**Fix.** Classify subpackages as keep/deprecate/remove, set an explicit supported Go range, replace standard-library duplicates, migrate tooling, and release a compatibility plan. Avoid a blanket syntax upgrade until consumers and semantic-versioning policy are known.
